The WikiWalk team is proposing edits to this page. The following edits proposed are to link two tales, In Dread Forever Fled and All They Want is the Blood to SCP-450. Both tales reference and link back to the SCP, and can be defined in portions of the SCP's description.

Proposing that the following be edited from this:

A complex pattern, drawn in human blood, is located on the wall behind the electric chair.

Lack of same is cause for concern.

To this:

A complex pattern, drawn in human blood, is located on the wall behind the electric chair.

Lack of same is cause for concern.

item.content:encoded:
Thanks for the suggestion! That was an interesting read.

It's fun to see I'm not the first to think along those lines, however, I wish the tale had 1. added more to the original article, and 2. delved more deeply into the way the containment procedures are obviously (probably) phony, for the reasons I've outlined in my first post above.

For all the emphasis the tale puts on the walking as the single most important part of the containment, it never asks WHY it matters so much, or WHAT makes it so effective. The tale's on the right track when it shows the blood pattern to be useless, but, seeing that the walk itself is an even more bizarre and arbitrary-seeming part of the containment procedure, it's a shame that its usefulness wasn't at least called into question by the characters.

Just my two cents.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
I'm oddly fascinated by this one… +1

Anyone else get this weird feeling that personnel are only being sent in as sacrifices to appease the ghosts? The security protocols seemed to have been put in place to make them easy targets (can't walk fast, should ignore the dead bodies that are a clear warning sign that they should turn around).

It's also not in the Foundation's nature not to elaborate on a special containment procedure (the maintaining of the blood pattern), which after all is the most important part of an SCP file in-universe, or to not at least to theorize on how the procedures work and why they're effective. This suggests to me that the blood pattern as a containment procedure is complete bullshit.

Notice also how the file doesn't explain, at all, how the pattern should be maintained, or whose blood should be used to do so - clearly maintaining the blood pattern is either irrelevant, or the ghosts maintain it themselves, for whatever reason, using the blood from the victims they're fed by the Foundation.

Of course, maybe there aren't any ghosts, and the prison is what feeds on people, or maybe it's something else entirely.

…I think I got the easter egg.

166.5 meters. 0.25 meters per second. 166.5m x 1s/0.25m = 666 seconds.

That can't be a coincidence. It's a sign that an SCP is well-written when putting the number "666" as an easter egg makes me like it more.

Or maybe I'm just late to the party and nobody even thought it worth mentioning. My ego hopes that that is not the case.
